# Architecture

How MNML is put together: a Home Assistant integration that serves the cards, their editors and their templates and installs the theme, all built from this repository and released as one `mnml.zip`. For how the cards behave, see [How the cards work](cards.md); for how they look, [Design](design.md); for the theme, [The theme](theme.md).

## The parts

- `src/contract/`: the contract (`cards.ts`, `entities.ts`, `templates.ts`) and what the cards and their users both read
- `src/interface/`: MNML's public interface as a record: `surface()`, `interface.json`, its diff and the release notes
- `src/cards/`: the cards, their base class, the known-key schemas, the registration and the loader, and `parts/`
- `src/ha/`: Home Assistant in the browser: the typed `hass`, formatting, names, rules, conditions, navigation, motion, the reading direction, and the template parts that draw Home Assistant's own elements
- `src/words/`: the cards' own words, and under `templates` the words the templates name, one table per language: `en.ts` is the source and `Words` its type, and `wordsFor()` picks by `hass.locale.language`, then its base language, then English
- `src/words/panel/`: the panel's and the card editors' words, apart from the cards' so the cards bundle does not carry them: `en.ts` (`PanelWords`) and `editors-en.ts` (`EditorWords`) are the sources, Romanian beside each; `panelWordsFor()` and `editorWordsFor()` pick through `pick()`, the full language, then its base, then English
- `src/store/`: the integration's template store in the browser, and the shipped families fetched on demand
- `src/editors/`: the card editors and their description vocabulary
- `src/panel/`: the MNML panel
- `src/templates/`: the template engine, discovery, the shipped templates' loader, the dashboard expander
- `templates/`: the shipped templates, one YAML file per family, and `shapes.yaml`, the slot shapes they share
- `src/home/`: the home generator: `Home` and its parts, `build()`, `drawn()` and `problems()`
- `src/builder/`: the dashboard builder: a plan's defaults from the home's registries, a person's slots, the plan a strategy's options make, and the dashboard a plan makes
- `src/strategy/`: the `custom:mnml` dashboard strategy, and its editor in Home Assistant's dashboard settings
- `demo/`: the demo home, Joe's and Jane's, its YAML, and the throwaway instance's entities for it
- `src/build/`: `buildBundle()`, and the command line that runs it
- `src/theme/`: the theme's model, its mapping onto Home Assistant's variables, its contrast claims, its YAML
- `src/test/`: the jsdom helpers and the fake Home Assistant connection the element tests use
- `tools/`: the throwaway Home Assistant, its look, walk and screenshot passes, the discovery corpus's snapshot of it (`corpus.ts`, `snapshot.ts`), the integration's icons, the wiki's pages, the release zip, hassfest in Docker (`hassfest.ts`), and the interface's part of the release notes (`notes.ts`)
- `custom_components/mnml/`: the integration, and in `www/` (built, git-ignored) everything it serves
- `tests/`: the integration's tests, and the example plans and changes the TypeScript tests judge too

## `src/contract/`: what the cards and their users both read

- `entities.ts`: the id types: `EntityId<Domain>` and one alias per domain (`LightId`, `SensorId`, ...), with `isEntityId()`, a domain, a dot and an object id in lower case, by which `MnmlCard` also finds the entities a configuration names, and `isLooseEntityId()`, any text with a dot, what the template engine's `entity` and `entities` kinds take
- `entities.ts` also holds `MdiIcon` and `isIcon()`, `PopupHash`, `Subnet`, `ServiceName` (a closed union of the services the cards call, and `isService()`, the shape of a service's name) and `Corners<T>` (front left, front right, rear left, rear right)
- `plan.ts`: `Plan`, what the panel's builder keeps for a dashboard it made: its title and icon, its rooms by area, its people by `person` entity, its cars by key, its system templates, each with the slots it overrides, its devices on cards of their own (`devices`, each `{ device, template }`), and how its pop-ups open. Optionally it also keeps each section's look (`SectionLook`: a title, an icon, and but for Devices and System a template; `lookOf()` gives a section's look with the defaults, `SECTION_LOOKS`), the sections' `order`, each once (`orderOf()` puts any left out after them, in `PLAN_ORDER`), and the Glances strip (`glances`, discovered, with overrides, or `spelled`). A room, person or system choice may be `spelled`, its slots alone with nothing discovered
- `plan.ts` also holds `isPlan()`, which refuses an unknown key at every level, `isPersonId()`, and `SYSTEM_TEMPLATES`, the templates the builder offers for the System section. `tests/plans.json` holds example plans, valid and not, that `isPlan()` and the integration's schema both judge the same way
- `cards.ts`: the configuration of every card: the public interface of MNML; see below
- `dashboard.ts`: the frame a dashboard is written in: `Dashboard`, its `View`s, their `Section`s and each section's `Card`s, what `build()` and the builder's `dashboardOf()` both return
- `structure.ts`: every card's structure and every part's, once: `CARD_STRUCTURES`, by card type, and the parts (`STATE_ITEM`, `CONTROL`, `LIST_ROW` and the parts only a card holds). A structure names its keys in the order a form places them, each with its kind, whether it is required, and its default where a form needs it. The kinds are `text`, `texts`, `number`, `share`, `flag`, a `choice` of values, `entity` and `entities` with their domains, `icon`, `popup`, `service`, `color`, `words`, `corners`, a `rule`, `summary`, a `part` or `parts` of another structure, and the `cards` and `slots` of the cards without a form. A part that comes in kinds is `tagged()` by its `type`, or `marked()` by a marker key, with a last kind for a value with no marker
- In `structure.ts`, `plain<T>()`, `tagged<T>()` and `marked<T>()` hold each structure to its interface in `cards.ts`: a key missing or extra, or required where the interface makes it optional, does not compile. `chooseVariant()` is the one choice of a kind for a value, for the cards' checks and for the editors. A structure holds no label: the cards derive their known keys from it (`src/cards/keys.ts`) and check their values against it (`required.ts`), and the editors derive their forms, with the labels of `src/editors/labels.ts`
- `required.ts`: `problemsOf(structure, value)`, every way a value breaks a structure, each named by its path (`controls[1].entity is required`). It finds a required key absent, `null` or `''`, and a value not of its key's kind. The kinds take a text, a list of texts, a finite number, the value a flag writes, one of a `choice`'s options or of the contract's colours, and a service such as `light.turn_on`. They also take an entity of the key's domains, a list of entities, four `corners`, a pop-up hash, `words` within their options, a `summary`, and a list of cards each with a `type`. Inside a `part`, a `rule` or each of a list's `parts`, it checks the same against that structure, and a part that comes in kinds against the kind `chooseVariant()` picks. `requireStructure()` throws them as one error
- `subnet.ts`: `ipv4()` and `subnetRange()`, by which the clients card groups and validates
- `templates.ts`: the template format's types (`Template`, with its `retired` slot paths, `SlotSpec`, `Rule`, `Kind`, `Value`) with `isTemplate()`, `isMapping()` and `isStorable()`, the shape the integration stores. A template's `title` and `icon` with `lookProblem()`, `templateTitle()`, `templateIcon()` and `templateWithLook()`, and the slot words `slotLabel()`, `pathLabel()` and `slotGroup()` (a mapping `card`, `popups` a list of mappings). `idOf()`, a list item's `id`, and `plainKey()`, a key without its `?` or `!`
- `templates.ts` also holds the reserved keys, `ITEM_KEYS` (`id`, `if`, `unless`, `each`, `as`), `TEMPLATE_KEYS` (those and `template` and `slots`) and `LAYOUT_KEYS` (what every card takes for its place: `grid_options`, `visibility`, `view_layout`, `layout_options`, `card_mod`). And the two comparisons, `sameValue()`, whatever the order of a mapping's keys, and `sameWritten()`, key order included, for a check of whether what was written changed; see [the template engine](#srctemplates-the-template-engine)
- `yaml.ts`: `toYaml()`, the YAML writer: YAML 1.1, with every string Home Assistant's loader or the panel would read as something else quoted ([The YAML writer](cards.md#the-yaml-writer))

### The contract, `cards.ts`

- **Cards:** `TileCard`, `EntityCard`, `HeaderCard`, `HeadingCard`, `ListCard` (with `ListRow`), `AgendaCard` (with `AgendaSource`), `MessagesCard`, `ClientsCard` (with `ClientNetwork` and `ClientFields`), `ReportCard`, `WeatherCard`, `GlancesCard` (with `Glance`), `ButtonCard`, `SelectCard`, `SliderCard`, `MediaCard`, `CarPlanCard`, `PopupsCard` (with `Popup` and `LovelaceCardConfig`, any card a pop-up holds) and `TemplateCard`.
- **A tile's or header's subject** is one of two variants: a literal `name` and `icon`, with an optional `entity`; or an `entity` whose name (its device's, with `label`) and icon the card shows, where an `icon` may still override the entity's.
- **`Item`:** an entity with its name, state line, popup and controls. `EntityCard` is an `Item` with a `type` and optional nested `items`: the rows its expander reveals. `TileCard.item` is an `Item` too.
- **Controls:** `toggle`, `slider`, `select`, `service`, `nav`, `indicator`, `status`, `tyres`, `scenes`, `messages`, `dismiss`.
- **`StateItem`:** one entry of a state line. It is one of seven variants: an entity's state, an `attribute`, a literal `text`, the `minutes` of a seconds counter, a timestamp as a `relative` time, the `serial` number of the entity's device, or the entity's `name`. `icon: true` puts the state icon in front.
- **Rules:** `StateRule` (`is` / `not`); `EntityRule`, which adds the `entity` it reads; and a `status` control's rules, which add the `entities` they watch, how the tooltip names and words them (`label`, `words`), and the `color` they give.
- **`Condition`:** Home Assistant's visibility conditions as its editor writes them: `state`, `numeric_state`, `screen`, `user`, `and` / `or` / `not`, and any other kind, which the server judges.

A card reads nothing the types don't declare, and a key it does not declare is an error (`src/cards/keys.ts`, below). Leave an optional key out to get its default, so the YAML reads as intent: `state` defaults to the entity's own state line on an entity card, and `when` to `{ is: ['on'] }` on a coloured control, pill or header. A list row is the exception: without `when` it is coloured whenever it is shown, so a flag's condition lives in its `show`, and a coloured value row spells its `when`.

A threshold that is a share of something says so in its name. `low_share` and `warn_share` on the `tyres` control, and `tyre_low_share` and `tyre_warn_share` on the car plan, are ratios of a tyre's target (0.9, 0.95). A list row's `low` and `critical` are absolute values in the entity's unit (20, 5 for a battery's percentage).

`cards.ts` is part of the public interface that `interface.json` records: a new key or card is a minor release; while MNML is 0.x a minor release may also rename or remove one, or change its meaning, with a line in the release notes on how to migrate ([Releases](#releases)), and from 1.0 that is a major release.

## `src/interface/`: the public interface

- `interface.ts`: `surface()`, MNML's public interface as plain sorted JSON, of the record format `FORMAT` (1), which it writes first, as `format`. It holds every card type and its keys, from `CARD_STRUCTURES` (`cardPaths()`): each key by its path, with its kind, `!` when it is required, its values in parentheses (a `choice`'s or `words`'s options, or what a flag writes when it is not `true`, `flag(device)`) and `=` its default where the structure gives one (`text = "data"`). A part's keys follow its key after a `.` (`fields.name`), a list's after `[]` (`rows[].entity`), and each kind of a part that comes in kinds is a path of its own, `tagged` or `marked`, its name in angle brackets (`controls[]<indicator>`, then `controls[]<indicator>.color`; `<otherwise>` for the kind with no marker; a header's `<name>.icon`). A card's `type` is the card's name in the record
- `interface.ts` also records every shipped template and its slots (each its kind, with `!` when it is required, an object's fields as dotted paths, `lights.group`), and every slot shape of `templates/shapes.yaml`, resolved, as dotted paths with kinds (`meter`, `meter.power`). It holds the theme's name and the `mnml-*` variables it writes. It holds the integration's domain, its options (the `CONF_*` of `const.py`) and its websocket commands: the `type` of each in `websocket.py`, read by `integrationOf()`, which fails when it reads fewer than `websocket.py` has `@websocket_api.websocket_command` decorators. And it holds the keys of `Home`, `Room`, `Person`, `Car`, `System` and `SectionTitles` (the key tables of `src/home/types.ts`)
- `interface.json`, at the root, is the interface as last recorded: `interface.test.ts` fails while the two differ, naming each entry removed, changed (a key's or a slot's kind, required flag, values or default) or added, until `pnpm run fix:interface` records it. `compare()` makes that diff between two records, and `notes()` writes it as the Markdown of the release notes from the record a tag holds; `readSurface()` reads a record, and gives nothing for one of another format, which `notes()` then says to compare by hand
- `main.ts`: `pnpm run fix:interface`: writes `interface.json` from `surface()`, formatted by oxfmt. It is deliberately not part of `pnpm fix`, so that a change to the interface is recorded on purpose.

## `src/cards/`: the cards

- `register.ts` is the bundle's entry. It defines twenty-three elements: the seventeen cards, the pop-up shell, `mnml-slider` (the slider of the slider card and of a slider control's overlay), `mnml-tooltip`, `mnml-card-note` (the note drawn in place of a card that cannot be drawn), and the dashboard strategy `ll-strategy-dashboard-mnml` with its editor `mnml-strategy-editor` ([`src/strategy/`](#srcstrategy-the-dashboard-strategy)). It lists the cards and the shell in `window.customCards`, and the strategy in `window.customStrategies`, which offers it under **Community dashboards** when a dashboard is added. Each card gets its `getStubConfig()` from `stubs.ts`, each but the pop-ups card its `getConfigElement()` from `edit.ts`, and the template card its `getEntitySuggestion()` from `stands.ts`. It skips a tag that is already defined, so a second copy of the bundle on one dashboard defines nothing and throws nothing.
- One file per card, named after it in kebab-case; `parts/` holds what several cards share, and the pieces a large card's file is split into.
- `keys.ts` and `schemas.ts`: a card's known keys are a `KeySchema`, which `keysOf()` derives from a structure of `src/contract/structure.ts`, a key that holds a part, a list of parts or a rule with the schema of that structure nested, and `cardKeysOf()` with the card's `type` too. A card names its structure (`structure()`), and its known keys are `cardKeysOf()` of it; `schemas.ts` holds the parts' `STATE_ITEMS`, `CONTROLS` and `LIST_ROW`. The structures are typed against `cards.ts`, so the schemas cannot drift from it. A union is checked against the one kind a value picks (`chooseVariant()`), which names only the keys that kind allows (not those it spells `never`): by its `type` for a control, and by a marker key for a state item, a glance, the select card, a header's or tile's subject and a message source. So a toggle with a `slider`, or a text with an `attribute`, is an unknown key too.
- In `keys.ts`, `requireCard()` checks a configuration against its card's structure before anything else, at every depth the structure describes. It checks the keys first, allowing at the top the layout keys Home Assistant and card-mod add (`grid_options`, `visibility`, `view_layout`, `layout_options`, `card_mod`). Then it checks the values (`src/contract/required.ts`): the required keys, each key's kind, the parts of a list and the kind of a part that comes in kinds. `MnmlCard.setConfig()`, the pop-up shell and the template card all run it, and a card's own `validate()` checks only what a structure cannot say: that a network's subnet is an IPv4 range (the clients card), and that a glance's `confirm` comes with `toggle: true`.

- `base.ts`: `MnmlCard<C>`, the base class of every card but the pop-up shell and the template card: the check of a configuration against the card's `structure()`, configuration, updates only for what the configuration names, holds and teardown, `notify()`, and the default grid size; `Host`, what a part a card draws is given. See [How the cards work](cards.md#lifecycle-of-a-card)
- `styles.ts`: the shared styles, as `css` values: `MOTION_STYLE`, `BASE_STYLE` (its `:host` holds the shared colours as custom properties, `--m-pill`, `--m-hover`, `--m-edge`, `--m-edge-strong`), `HEADING_STYLE`, `ROW_STYLE`, `CONTROL_STYLE`
- `edit.ts`: `editorOf(tag)`, each card's `getConfigElement()`: it imports the editors' file by the URL `src/editors/where.ts` gives, and after a failed import asks for it again under a new URL (`?attempt=<n>`), since a browser keeps a failed dynamic import for the page
- `stubs.ts`: `STUBS`, each card's `getStubConfig()`, with a fitting entity of the home where the card takes one; `placeOf()`, where in the home a template fits best, which the gallery reads too
- `loader.ts`, `started.ts`, `iconset.ts`: The loader, its own entry, and the `mnml` icon set it registers; see [Why a loader](#custom_componentsmnml-the-integration)
- `template.ts`: `MnmlTemplateCard`, a template expanded in place ([Templates](templates.md#how-it-runs))
- `popups.ts`: `MnmlPopupsCard`, the pop-up shell ([How the cards work](cards.md#the-pop-up-shell))
- `parts/popup-unfold.ts`: the unfold geometry: `placed()`, `folded()`, `foldTo()`, `unfolded()`, `settled()`, `reveal()`, and `following()`, which keeps an unfolded pop-up on its origin. A scroll of the page or of any shadow root around the origin, a resize of the window, or a change of size that a `ResizeObserver` sees on the origin or an element around it starts a frame loop that places the pop-up again. The loop stops once the pop-up has stayed put for 6 frames, so an open pop-up costs nothing while the page is still
- `parts/popup-swipe.ts`: `swipeToClose()`, the swipe down that closes a pop-up, on its panel in every opening
- `parts/item.ts`: `itemRow()`, an item's row; `itemLine()`, the same item minified into one line, as a tile draws it; and `linkTo()`, a way into a pop-up, with `ITEM_STYLE`; used by the entity, tile, header and media cards
- `parts/section.ts`: `heading()` and `section()`, with `SECTION_STYLE`. The list, agenda, clients and car plan cards use `section()` so that their title stands above their surface, like a heading card above a card
- `parts/controls.ts`: a lane of controls: `renderControls()` and `controlsOf()`; a toggle or service control with a `confirm` rule acts through `parts/confirm.ts`
- `parts/confirm.ts`: the `confirm` key: `asks()`, whether the entity's state matches the control's `confirm` rule; `confirmed()`, by which the first press then arms the control for 3 s instead of acting, and only a second press while it is armed acts; `isArmed()` and `ask()`, the words an armed control shows and speaks in place of its tooltip (`Unlock? Tap again`). An arming is kept per card and per control, as a teardown the card holds, so a new configuration or the card leaving the page ends it. The toggle and service controls use it, and so does a glance with `toggle: true`
- `parts/slider.ts`: the slider: `MnmlSlider` (`mnml-slider`), `openSliderOverlay()`, `OVERLAY_STYLE`
- `parts/slider-spec.ts`: `sliderSpec()` per `SliderKind`: the range, the value, the commit and the gradient of each kind, as `SliderSpec`
- `parts/menu.ts`: the dropdown: `modeChoice()`, `optionChoice()`, `sceneChoice()`, `openMenu()`, `MENU_STYLE`
- `parts/overlay.ts`: `dismissable()`, which holds a card while its menu or slider overlay is open, and closes it on a tap outside or on Escape
- `parts/tooltip.ts`: `MnmlTooltip` (`mnml-tooltip`), the one tooltip of the cards, and `createTips()`, which makes the `tip()` directive that puts it on an element, in place of the browser's `title`, and `tipOf()`, the text an element was given. The module's `tip()` and `tipOf()` are the page's; a test makes its own. A mouse shows it on hover and a keyboard on focus. On touch, a press held 500 ms opens it and does not act, since the click that ends the press and the context menu are swallowed, while moving off the element or lifting sooner lets go, and the next touch anywhere closes it. A short press acts as before
- `parts/popup-registry.ts`: `createPopupRegistry()`: `announce()`, `withdraw()`, `announced()`, `onAnnounce()`, the pop-ups template cards give the shell. The module's are the page's, the one the cards and the shell share; a test makes its own. `checkPopups()`
- `parts/card-element.ts`: `cardOf()`, a card's element: an MNML card made by its own class, a Home Assistant card by its card helpers when the page has them, or else an `MnmlCardNote` (`mnml-card-note`) that says why; an `error` card, and an MNML card that refuses its configuration, are a note with the reason. The template card, the pop-up shell, the gallery and the panel draw their cards with it

## `src/ha/` and `src/store/`: Home Assistant in the browser

- `ha/hass.ts`: the typed subset of `hass` the cards use, state readers (`stateOf`, `hasValue`, `isUnavailable`, `isOn`, `numericState`, ...) and `callService()`, `toggleEntity()`, `run()` and `settled()`, which turn a failed call into Home Assistant's toast; `callApi()` is the one REST call, the agenda's calendar events; `connection` reads and follows the store
- `ha/registries.ts`: the registries' types, which import nothing: `Registries`, what discovery reads, its `AreaEntry` (with the `aliases` the area assistant reads), `DeviceEntry` (a device's maker, model, `entry_type` and `via_device_id`, which discovery reads) and `EntityEntry`, and `EnergyPrefs`, the energy settings a snapshot may carry
- `ha/snapshot.ts`: `registriesOf()`, the snapshot discovery reads of a `hass`: its areas, devices, entities and states, and its energy settings once they are known
- `ha/energy.ts`: `energyPrefs(connection)`, Home Assistant's energy settings (`energy/get_prefs`) as discovery reads them: each source's type, power (`stat_rate`) and charge (`stat_soc`), each metered device's total, power and the device it is part of; none when the home has none or the answer is not a mapping. It asks once per connection, every reader sharing the answer, so a change to the settings shows after a reload; `knownEnergy(connection)` is the answer once it is in, which `registriesOf()` adds. The panel and the strategy wait for it, and a template card asks and draws again when it comes
- `ha/templates.ts`: the template parts: `icon()`, `stateIcon()`, `attributeIcon()` and `relativeTime()`, Home Assistant's own elements; `colorVar()` and `colorStyle()`, a `Color` as `--m-color`; `onPress()`, Enter and Space as a press; `quietly()`, a handler that stops its event
- `ha/part.ts`: `partName()`, the `_part` the engine marks a drawn piece with, which the base card and the panel's preview read, and `partOf()`, the same for a `data-part` attribute, `nothing` when there is none
- `ha/rules.ts`: `normalise()`, `matches()`, `shown()`, `active()`, `tint()`, `tyreBand()`, and `UNAVAILABLE`, the colour of an offline entity
- `ha/names.ts`: `entityName()`, `nameOf()`, `cardName()` (a card's `name`, else its entity's), `deviceSerial()`
- `ha/format.ts`: `formatState()`, `formatAttribute()`, `stateLine()`, and `unavailableValue()`, the orange dash
- `ha/conditions.ts`: `Judge`, which judges a card's `visibility` as Home Assistant's frontend does, in the browser or through `subscribe_condition`, for a pop-up's cards and a template card's drawn card; and `conditionProblem()`
- `ha/timer.ts`: `countdown()`, `clock()`, `secondsOf()`, `isTimer()` and `timerPresets()`
- `ha/messages.ts`: `Message`, `Repair`, `notificationFeed()`, `repairFeed()` and `repairMessage()`
- `ha/message-count.ts`: `messageCount()`, the number of Home Assistant's notifications and an administrator's repairs, one subscription to each shared by every card that counts them
- `ha/navigation.ts`: `navigate()`, `closePopup()`, `back()`, `prebuild()`
- `ha/direction.ts`: `rightToLeft()`, the nearest `dir` through shadow roots, for what CSS cannot mirror: the header's back arrow, the slider, the menu's side and the pop-ups' slide
- `ha/motion.ts`: `reduced()`, `narrow()`, `leave()`
- `ha/card-helpers.ts`: `ChildCard`, a card drawn inside another, by `cardOf()` or by Home Assistant's `loadCardHelpers().createCardElement()`, and the type of `window.loadCardHelpers`
- `ha/field.ts`: `field()`, one key of a value of unknown shape, without a cast
- `store/store.ts`: the integration's store in the browser. `sharedTemplates(connection)` subscribes to `mnml/templates/subscribe` once per connection, without the library's automatic resubscribe, and again after each reconnect. While the integration loads it tries again every 5 seconds for 5 minutes; an unknown command on a first subscription, or a store the integration could not read, is an empty store. An entry with a change of an unknown shape is left out whole. `resolvedTemplates()` gives the order a card, its editor and the panel read templates in: the home's own, a shipped one with its changes, the shipped. `knownShared()` and `onShared()`. `createStore()` makes one store; the module's `sharedTemplates()`, `knownShared()` and `onShared()` are the page's, and a test makes its own
- In `store/store.ts`, the ready state holds the home's own templates with the shapes they name resolved (one that cannot be resolved, for any reason, is kept as written and reported on the console, so only the cards that draw it fail), `written`, the own templates as stored, for the panel, and the changes
- `store/shipped.ts`: the shipped templates in the browser: `createShipped(load, owner, common)`, and `SHIPPED_TEMPLATES`, the page's own: `templates()` (common and what is loaded), `later()`, `need(names)` (each family fetched once, in parallel) and `failure(names)`; a family that is missing (404, or 410) stays failed for the page, and one that failed otherwise may be fetched again after 30 seconds

## `src/editors/`: the card editors

The card editors are a file of their own, loaded the first time a card is edited ([Editing in the UI](editors.md)). Editors and panel parts are `LitElement`s; the rest draws `html` templates.

- `main.ts`: the editors' entry: it loads `ha-form`, then defines `mnml-card-editor`, `mnml-template-card-editor`, `mnml-template-gallery`, `mnml-row-menu`, `mnml-words` and `mnml-related`
- `form.ts`: the vocabulary of a form: `Field`, `PlainForm` (its fields, sections, labels and help) and `ChoiceForm` (its kinds), `Form` either, with `checkValue()`, `cleanValue()`, `place()`, `switchVariant()`, `variantOf()` and `starter()`
- `cards.ts`: `describer()`, which makes the description of a form (a `Form` of `form.ts`) from a structure of `src/contract/structure.ts` and a table of labels. A description has a field of each key, of the key's kind, a colour or service field with its list, and a part with a description of its own. `DESCRIPTIONS` holds every card with a form, which is every card but the pop-ups and template cards
- `labels.ts`: `LABELS`, by the name of each structure the editors draw: the label of the card or part and of each of its kinds, the label of a key whose humanised name reads badly, their help under the field, and its sections, the panels of its form (one, under its label, when it gives none)
- `lists.ts`: the choices of a field the structure leaves to the editors: the services, held to `ServiceName`, the corner names, and the contract's colours
- `ha-form-data.ts`: Home Assistant's form and back: `schemaOf()`, `formData()`, `fromForm()`, which writes only the fields the form changed, `slotsFromForm()`, which writes `null` for an emptied slot that has a default
- `draw.ts`: the drawing. `Lens` is the `get()` and `set()` of the value a form edits, the card itself or a part or item in it. `objectForm()` draws a part or card in its sections or whole, with the kind switch, and `keysForm()` its keys, the simple ones in one form and each list or part in its own. `formOf()` draws the simple keys in one form, with an optional helper line and reader, which the template card's slots use, and `adder()` an Add button
- `drawing.ts`: `Drawing`, how an edit is drawn: `REDRAW`, the form drawn again (a part added, a kind switched), or `IN_PLACE`, the form left as it is, so the field being typed in keeps its focus. A `Lens`'s `set()`, the panel's edits and the words editor take one
- `ha-form.ts`: `haForm()`, Home Assistant's `ha-form`, and `loadHaForm()`, which asks a built-in card for its editor so that `ha-form` is defined; `formMissing()`, what to do when `ha-form` is not defined, said once
- `panel.ts`: `sectionPanel()`, a section as Home Assistant's expansion panel or a look-alike, drawn when first opened
- `row-menu.ts`: `MnmlRowMenu` (`mnml-row-menu`), a part's three-dot menu, and `rowMenu()`, which draws one
- `words.ts`: `MnmlWords` (`mnml-words`), the pairs of a state and its word, or of a state and its colour, which keeps the boxes as typed while two states clash
- `related.ts`: `MnmlRelated` (`mnml-related`), around the fields of a template card's `object` slot. Given a device (`Related`: the device's own entities, its `via_device` relatives and its area, the three tiers the pickers rank by), it answers the `context-request` of Home Assistant's entity pickers inside it for their `related` context, the one Home Assistant's frontend orders a picker's entities by. It tells them again when the device changes, a value holding the same ids being no change. Without a device, and for any other context, the request goes on to Home Assistant
- `summary.ts`: `summarize()`, a panel's summary; one part counts as "1 control", by `singular()`
- `icons.ts`, `clipboard.ts`, `style.ts`: A panel's icon by its title; the part last copied, in the browser's storage; `EDITOR_STYLE`
- `card-editor.ts`: `MnmlCardEditor`, the editor of every card with keys
- `template-card.ts`: `MnmlTemplateCardEditor`, the template card's editor: where the values come from (an area, the whole home or the card) and the slot forms, the ties of a slot's own rule, and for an `object` slot filled from a device the device, **Use another** (`fromDevice()`) and its fields inside `mnml-related`; it keeps the gallery cached across Change. **Edit this template** asks Only this card or Every card, and a module flag remembers Every card while the page is open
- `gallery.ts`: `MnmlTemplateGallery` (`mnml-template-gallery`), the gallery: the filter, the fold, the home's own templates first, and inert live previews drawn as they scroll into view, each given every new `hass`; it fires `template-picked`, and holds its own styles. When a tile finds nothing in the home (`placeOf()`) and `unplaced()` counts something, a line above the tiles links to the area assistant
- `fill.ts`: where a template card's values come from (an area, the whole home or the card), its notes ("Found in Living", "Found: Roborock S8 in Living", "Not set"), `deviceIn()`, the device of those that fit that holds most of a value's entities, and its panels
- `slots.ts`: a template's slots as a shape, and its preview
- `popup-names.ts`: `popupChoices()`, pop-ups named by their headers, for the pop-up picker and the preview
- `leave.ts`: `openPanel()`, which closes Home Assistant's card dialog, asking first when the card has changes, and opens the MNML panel
- `where.ts`: `EDITORS`, the URL of the editors' file, which the build fills in

## `src/panel/`: the MNML panel

The panel is a file of its own, `mnml-cards-panel.js`, which the integration registers ([The MNML panel](editors.md#the-mnml-panel)).

- `main.ts`: `MnmlPanel` (`mnml-panel`): the routing, the state, the websocket reads and the page: the toolbar and the Dashboards and Templates tabs, then the dashboards (at `/mnml` and `/mnml/dashboards`), a dashboard's builder, the library (at `/mnml/templates`), a template's builder, or the area assistant (at `/mnml/areas`); `PAGE_STYLE`. The area assistant's host asks before each write, keeps the undo record while the panel is open, and returns to where the assistant was opened from
- `library-actions.ts`: the library's flows over a `LibraryHost` (`call`, the dialogs, the state, `refresh`, `save`, `download`): new, duplicate, history, export, import (a file, or the dashboards' templates), delete or reset, and rename with its references (`drawFates()`, `saveTemplate()`)
- `dashboard-actions.ts`: the dashboards' flows over a `DashboardHost` (the library's host, `go` and `visit`): quick start (which first offers the area assistant when more than half of what a room would show is in no area), create or rebuild (whose question lists `changesIn()`, named by `rowNames()`), undo, forget, share, from a template, and the offer to open
- `message.ts`: `messageOf()`, an error as a sentence
- `building.ts`: the dashboards MNML built and Home Assistant's own, read (`builtOf()`, `boardsOf()`); a new dashboard's address (`addressFor()`). And each change as the messages it sends, in order: `makeDashboard()` (keep the plan, create, save the cards; a create Home Assistant refuses lets the plan go again), `rebuildDashboard()` (read the cards it replaces, stopping on anything but no cards yet; keep the plan with the replaced version; save the cards; retitle), `undoDashboard()` and `forgetDashboard()`
- `dashboards.ts`: `MnmlDashboards`, the Dashboards tab: the list, each row with Open, Undo, Share and Forget, or the offer to build one, by Quick start, Step by step or From a template
- `share.ts`: what a shared dashboard template makes here (`previewOf()`, `summary()`), and the names its templates come in under (`settled()`, over the library's `settleImport()`)
- `plan-editor.ts`: `MnmlPlanEditor`, a dashboard's builder: the plan as a draft, its sections, Customize on each row with the check that its card still draws, Add a car, and the check before a save. Its Glances section turns the Glances strip on or off. Its Devices section, drawn by `plan-devices.ts`, lists the devices a template stands for by area, each ticked onto a card of its own, with the room that already shows it. Its Rooms section's no-area line opens the area assistant through `PlanHost.sortAreas`. Parts on a row of a room, person or system card that is not spelled lists the tile's parts from `partsOf()` as chips that hide a part or show it again, with Swap from `swapsFor()` beside a part that is one entity; `plan-devices.ts` adds Same for another device to a device ticked. `PLAN_STYLE`, its sections' and rows' styles, draws the area assistant too
- `areas.ts`: `MnmlAreas` (`mnml-areas`), the area assistant ([Sorting the home into areas](editors.md#sorting-the-home-into-areas)): the suggestions grouped by area, each group's room tile drawn inert over the registries as they would be (`placedRegistries()`), the ticks, and Assign and Undo through its `AreasHost`
- `area-writes.ts`: `assignAreas(call, suggestions, registries)` makes the new areas (`config/area_registry/create`), then places each device and entity (`config/device_registry/update`, `config/entity_registry/update`). It returns the undo record, each area made and each subject's area before, with the first failure; a failure making an area stops before anything is placed
- `area-writes.ts` also holds `undoAreas()`, which puts each subject back, then deletes the areas made once all are back, and `joinedUndo()`, which joins two records, keeping each subject's earliest area
- `plan-edits.ts`: the plan editor's pure edits: `movedBy()`, `sectionsWithLook()`, `withDeclared()`, `withOrder()`, `withSystem()`, `trimmed()`, `templatesOf()`, `withGlances()`, `withDevice()` (a ticked device in the list's order), `withoutDevice()`, `slotsWith()` (a row's slot set, set to none or dropped) and `roomName()`. `changesIn()` gives the changes since the build as `PlanChange`s: a field, a row added, removed or changed with its name from `RowNames`, or a section's new order. `planChanges()` counts them
- `live-card.ts`: `MnmlLiveCard`, one card drawn with `cardOf()`, drawn again only when its configuration changes
- `customize.ts`: `customize()`, the template card's editor on one card in a dialog, loaded as Home Assistant loads it (the card's `getConfigElement()`); **Done** runs the caller's check and keeps the dialog open with its reason
- `data.ts`: the library's rows (`rowsOf()`, `usesOf()`, `describe()`), a template's draft (`draftOf()`), what a template is kept as (`Entry`, `entryOf()`, `roundTrips()`, `storedAs()`) and the panel's state (`PanelState`). A home template as written and readable: `shapedOf()` resolves a written template's slot shapes, `readableOf()` a draft for discovery and the pickers, `slotOf()` one written slot
- `library.ts`: `MnmlLibrary`
- `template-builder.ts`: `MnmlBuilder`: the header, the draft with undo and redo, the tabs and the save; it lists the style sheets of its parts
- `conflicts.ts`, `edited-here.ts`: The box of a release's conflicts; a shared piece edited here, copied into the template (`editedHereOf()`, `withEditedHere()`)
- `outline.ts`: a card's or the pop-ups' tree of parts (`outlinePart()`, `groupOf()`, `drawOutline()`) and the parts a draft changed (`changedParts()`)
- `simple.ts`: `simpleOf()`, a template's parts as rows (switchable when in a list, with their conditions and their literal looks, a fragment's slots included), what switching one off and on keeps, and `drawLook()`, one look as a field
- `stage-panel.ts`: the Design tab's panel: the crumbs, the part's looks, its switch, its moves, what can be added to it, and the inspector under All settings
- `binding.ts`: the entities a part reads (`dataFields()`), what a slot is called and whether it finds itself, and the edits behind the panel's pickers: the entity of a part, a preview value in the example, a slot made from the entity picked (`automateField()`), an entity written in place of a slot
- `picks.ts`: what was picked in the Design tab for the preview of a template, kept in the browser, template by template
- `starters.ts`: the starting points of a new template: a tile, a list, a strip of statuses, a pop-up, each with entities of the home, and the screen that offers them (`drawStarters()`)
- `inspector.ts`: `drawInspector()`, a part's fields, bindings and condition
- `binder.ts`: `MnmlBinder`, which binds a field to a slot of a kind that fits it (`fittingSlots()`)
- `preview.ts`: `MnmlPreview`, a draft expanded (`tryDraft()`) and drawn with `cardOf()`. In the Design tab it is the stage: the expansion is marked, a click picks the part under the pointer, and boxes outline the hovered and the picked parts
- `slots-tab.ts`: `drawSlots()`, the slots and their rules as sentences
- `yaml.ts`: `MnmlYaml`, the YAML tab, and `readYaml()`
- `check.ts`: `problemOf()`, the check before a save
- `transfer.ts`: import, export, the dashboards' `mnml_templates:` (`dashboardTemplates()`, `notKept()`) and renames
- `tree.ts`: paths of keys and `#<id>`s in a template (`valueAt()`, `withValue()`, `listAt()`), `movedTo()`, `uniqueId()`, which gives a part a `my-` id, and `adoptIds()`
- `dialog.ts`, `form.ts`, `lovelace.ts`, `style.ts`: `dialogsOn()`, the dialogs (ask, confirm, a name, a file or pasted YAML); a small `ha-form`; Home Assistant's Lovelace module, loaded on the panel's page through `partial-panel-resolver`'s `_getRoutes()` so that `ha-form` can load; `PANEL_STYLE`, the controls several elements share (each element adds its own)

## `src/templates/`: the template engine

[Templates](templates.md) is the language; this is how it is built.

- `expand.ts`: `expand(templates, instance, discovered, later, marking, words)` returns `{ card, popups }` and touches nothing else. A name in `later`, a shipped template not loaded yet, is drawn as nothing and listed in `missing`, so one pass names every family a card still needs; a name in neither is an error. It checks each template's slots once (known kinds, lower-case names, no shape left unresolved). It resolves each slot (the instance's value, else the discovered one, else the default) and checks its kind and its fields. Then it renders the template's tree: `[[path]]`, with `*`, `?field` and `!field` projecting a path over a list, `each`/`as`, `if`/`unless`, nested `template:` with `slots:`, keys ending in `?` (dropped when empty) or `!` (a list that keeps every place, an unfilled one as `null`), lists spliced. A mistake is a `TemplateError` naming the template and the path, and its `said`, the mistake in the words of the slot labels, for the panel and the template card's note.
- In `expand.ts`, a fifth argument of `expand()`, a marking (`{ singles }`), makes the expansion write `_part`, the path of the part (`card/chips/#window`, the same path the outline and `valueAt()` use). It writes it on every item of a list with an id, on the card, and on each single part the marking names, never inside a fragment, and never where it would be added to a list. The Design tab's stage reads it; the cards carry it as `data-part` on what they draw (`ha/part.ts`) and take it as a key of every part, drawing nothing different.
- `expand()` checks a template's `retired` paths once (dotted slot paths, none of them declared), takes a value given for a retired path and ignores it, and allows `?field` and `!field` only over a list of objects. `words`, a table's `templates` group (English when none is given), fills `[[words.<name>]]`; it checks every word of a template once, drawn or not, and refuses a slot or an `as:` named `words`. `toValue()` copies JSON-like data into a `Value`, so a TypeScript caller converts its interfaces once, without a cast.
- `changes.ts`: `applyChanges(template, changes)` lays the home's changes over a shipped template (set, remove, insert, move, by a path of keys and `#<id>`s) and says which are changed or gone, judged against the shipped template. `isChange()` checks a change's shape for its op as the integration's schema does: every key its op takes and no other, and every path segment, `key`, `id` and `after` a non-empty name that is not `__proto__`, `constructor` or `prototype`. `tests/changes.json` holds example changes, valid and not, that `changes.test.ts` and `tests/test_store.py` both judge. `baseOf()` is the hash a change's `base` holds, of what it touches, and `nodeHash()` is the stable hash under it. `changesOf(base, edited)` works out the changes from a shipped template to an edit of it. An `id:` on a list item is a control key to `expand()`, so no card sees it; `ids.test.ts` holds every part of a shipped card or pop-up to one, unique in its list.
- `ids.ts`, `ids.json`, `ids-main.ts`: every released part path, and the retired ones; `pnpm run fix:ids` (part of `pnpm fix`) adds new parts, and `ids.test.ts` fails on one gone without being retired, and on a shipped id that starts with `my-`, the prefix of the ids the panel gives.
- `catalog.ts`, `catalog-main.ts`: `catalogText()`, [the catalog](catalog.md) of the shipped templates from `templates/*.yaml`: each family, each template's title, icon and description, its slots as a table, the rules that find them in words, its retired slots, and the pop-ups it brings, directly, through its cards and through its pop-ups' cards. A slot whose rule is its shape's points to the shape. `pnpm run fix:docs` (part of `pnpm fix`) writes it, aligned as oxfmt and markdownlint want it, and `docs.test.ts` fails while it is stale.
- `discover.ts`: `discover(template, area, registries, device?)` fills the slots that have a rule, from the areas, devices, entities and states it is given, and Home Assistant's energy settings when the snapshot has them. With no area, only the `scope: all` rules and the energy values. On a device, only the device and its `via_device` relatives, the device's name and slug standing in for the area's. It is pure too; the template card hands it `hass`'s registries.
- `energy.ts`: the `energy.*` rule values, read from the snapshot's energy settings wherever the rule sits. `energy.grid_power`, `energy.solar_power` and `energy.battery_power` are each source of that type's `stat_rate`, and `energy.battery_charge` a battery's `stat_soc`; an `entity` slot takes the first, an `entities` slot every one. `energy.devices` is each metered device with a power, as an object of `power` (its `stat_rate`) and `total` (its `stat_consumption`), as far as the slot declares those fields, or as their powers for an `entity` or `entities` slot. A statistic that names no entity of the snapshot is left out, so is a device inside another listed one (its `included_in_stat`, followed up), whose power the other already counts. A step of an energy rule says so in words, is noted as home-wide, and says why when it finds nothing (`missing`).
- `discover.ts` hands one search context down the rules, `Search`, in place of a row of parameters: the registries and their index, where it looks (an area, a device, one entity, a device's relatives and the ones already claimed), the slot path a step is noted under, and the recorder. It also holds the label override (`discoverSlot()` looks for `mnml_<slot>` before the rules) and `fromDevice(spec, device, area, registries)`, an `object` slot filled from a device given by the slot's field rules, as its anchor or its label fills it, which the card editor's **Use another** writes.
- `entity-index.ts`: `indexOf(registries)`, the registries indexed once per snapshot, in a `WeakMap` keyed by the entities and checked against the same devices and areas. It holds the visible entities sorted by id once, and grouped by domain, id, area (the entity's own, else its device's), device and label (the entity's or its device's). It also holds each device's integrations, hidden entities included, the areas by name, and each device's `via_device` children. A rule filters a short list that is already sorted, not every entity. `areaOf()`, `deviceOf()`, `deviceName()` (a device's name as Home Assistant shows it), `byDeviceName()` and `relativesOf()` (a device's `via_device` parent and children, kept in the index once found) go with it.
- `filters.ts`: the filters, as one table of predicates. For each key of a `Filter` (`domain`, `device_class`, `platform`, `translation_key`, `entity_category`, `unit`, `state_class`, `attribute`, `name`, `manufacturer`, `model`, `entry_type`, `integration`, `label` and `exclude`) it holds whether an entity passes, why it does not, and the filter in words. `matches()`, `whyNot()` (the near misses of `explain()`), `describe()`, and `filterWords()` and `TEXT_FILTERS` (the keys the panel offers, whose English words in the panel's table a test holds to these) all come from that table, and the builder's room marks are filters too, so matching, its reasons and the marks cannot read a filter differently.
- `explain.ts`: `explain(template, area, registries, device?)` returns, per slot with a rule, the value and the steps taken, and for an empty slot a reason. A `Step` holds the slot's field it is for, `''` for the slot itself, the rule in words, the entities that matched, best first, the ones picked, and the ones tied with the best. For an anchored rule it holds the devices that hold a match and the ones taken. It also holds the near misses and why they missed, and why an energy rule found nothing. For an `object` slot, `devices` are the devices (`DeviceFit`: id, name, area's name) that the slot's own anchor or label found and that fill it, and `device` the one chosen; a step inside the slot offers none. It runs `discover()`'s own code with a recorder, so the two cannot disagree.
- `rank.ts`: `fitOf(template, scope, registries)`, what a template finds in an area, on a device or in the whole home, whether it fills every required slot, and how many slots it fills beyond the area's name, id and icon (`fillsHome`). `byFit` ranks fits, complete first, then the most; `bestFit` picks the best place. The gallery's previews, the Design tab and the suggestions rank with it.
- `stands.ts`: the template index (`templateIndex`: each template that stands for a device, with its anchor, the slots it discovers, its title and icon, and `room`), `cardsFor(device)`, `devicesFor(template)` and `suggestionsFor(entity)`, Home Assistant's card suggestions.
- `template-index.ts`: `TEMPLATE_INDEX`, the shipped templates' index; in the bundle `src/build/bundle.ts` replaces it with the data, so a suggestion loads no family.
- `corpus.ts`, `corpus/`, `corpus-main.ts`: the discovery corpus. `corpus/*.json` are registries (areas, devices, entities, states). `tidy`, `messy`, `labelled`, `systems` and `devices` are written by hand to hold what real homes do: two matches for one slot, a hidden entity, a device with no area, an entity whose own area beats its device's. `labelled` adds the `mnml_` labels a user puts on entities. `systems` has no areas, and the devices of the system integrations, Proxmox, UniFi, Tailscale and the media servers. `devices` has a room's richer devices: a robot vacuum and its dock, an air conditioner, a radiator's thermostat and a heater with no device, metered and plain plugs, a 3D printer, a speaker and a washer. `demo` is a snapshot of the throwaway Home Assistant (`pnpm run corpus:demo`, which only ever reads a local instance).
- `corpus/expected.json` is what every shipped template discovers in every area of every home; `corpus.test.ts` fails when that changes, and `pnpm run accept:corpus` accepts the change, to be read in the diff. It is not part of `pnpm fix`, so a change in what discovery finds is always a decision.
- `tools/snapshot.ts` keeps what discovery and the builder read. Of each area it keeps its name, icon, and temperature and humidity entities, and of each device its names, maker, model, `entry_type`, `via_device_id` and labels. Of each enabled entity it keeps its device, area, platform, `translation_key`, own name, `entity_category`, whether it is hidden, and its labels. Of each state it keeps the attributes the rules filter on: `device_class`, `friendly_name`, `unit_of_measurement`, `state_class`, `hvac_modes`, `device_trackers` (a person's) and `source_type`.
- `shipped.ts`: `readTemplates()` reads `templates/*.yaml` with `yaml`, refusing a name defined twice; `SHIPPED` is what it read, for the generator and the tests. `familyNames()` and `readFamily()` read one file, a family, at a time, its shapes resolved; `readShapes()` reads `templates/shapes.yaml`, which is no family.
- `slot-shapes.ts`: `withShapes(name, template, shapes)` writes out every slot and field that names a shape ([Shapes](templates.md#writing-a-template)): the shape's spec with the slot's own keys over it, a list of it for `kind: objects`, and the fields it changes. The template types as written, before their shapes are resolved, are `WrittenSlot` and `WrittenTemplate` in `src/contract/templates.ts`. It leaves a template that names no shape as it is, and a slot or field that is not a mapping to the engine's own checks; a mistake is a `TemplateError` naming the template, the slot and the shapes it goes through.
- `families.ts`: the families as the browser gets them: `COMMON`, the shared fragments of `common.yaml`; `OWNER`, the family of every other name; `SIZES`, the literal card type and `grid_options` of each family template, for sizing a card before its family arrives; `SLOT_SHAPES`, the shipped slot shapes, which the store resolves the home's own templates with; and `loadFamily(family)`. In Node it reads the YAML. In the bundle a rolldown plugin in `src/build/bundle.ts` replaces it, with `COMMON`, `OWNER`, `SIZES` and `SLOT_SHAPES` as data, every family's JSON file written with its shapes resolved, and a `loadFamily()` that fetches the family's JSON file next to the bundle, so the browser carries no YAML parser.
- `family-titles.ts`: `familyTitle()`, each family's title, for the library and the gallery.
- `edit-here.ts`: `editHere(use, templates, taken)`, the copy of a template use behind **Edit it here**: what the used template draws, its slots replaced by what the use gave them (a reference to a slot of the template around stays one), its conditions and loops renamed to match, its pop-ups returned. It gives up on what cannot be copied, and `edit-here.test.ts` copies every use of every shipped template and checks that the demo home draws as before.
- `roles.ts`: `rolesOf(templates)`, each template a tile, a pop-up or a part ([Roles](templates.md#roles)), for the library and the gallery, and `namesIn()`, every template a value uses, which a dashboard template also gathers its templates by.
- `dashboard.ts`: `expandDashboard(templates, config)` expands every template card of a dashboard and gathers their pop-ups into its popups card, in document order: what a dashboard of templates draws, without a browser. An instance's layout keys (`grid_options`, `visibility`, `view_layout`, `layout_options`, `card_mod`) stay on the card it expands to; its `area` is not read, so the card has only what the instance spells.
- `overrides.ts`: `overridesOf(found, values)`, what a card's values change of what discovery found: the editor and the builder both write it.

The template format's types are `src/contract/templates.ts`, part of the public interface beside `cards.ts`.

## `src/home/`: the home generator

A whole dashboard from one typed object: [The home dashboard](home.md) says what it draws.

- `types.ts`: `Home` and its parts (`Room`, `Lights`, `Heating`, `Ac`, `Person`, `Car`, `System` and the rest), every entity spelled with its domain's id type. It is public interface, as the contract is. `HOME_KEYS`, `ROOM_KEYS`, `PERSON_KEYS`, `CAR_KEYS`, `SYSTEM_KEYS` and `SECTION_TITLES_KEYS` name the keys of `Home`, `Room`, `Person`, `Car`, `System` and `SectionTitles`, whose sections, like `order`, are the builder's `SectionKey`s, each a `Record<keyof T, true>`, so the compiler rejects a table that misses a key or names one the type lacks; `interface.json` records them. It records the keys of those six types only, not of the types inside them (`Lights`, `Vacuum`, `Proxmox`, ...): a change to one of those fails a home's type check where the home spells it, and the release notes name it by hand.
- `slots.ts`: one function per subject from its part of the home to its template's slots, in snake_case: `roomSlots()`, `proxmoxSlots()`, `systemSlots()`, `glancesSlots()` and `snake()`, which the others, a person, a car and the systems, take as they are. It computes only what a template cannot: the room's joined, sorted batteries, the server's message sources, the system's firmware per room, and the home-wide lists of the Glances strip. A list that only gathers a field of another slot's list is a projection in the template (`[[devices.*.update]]`), not a slot.
- `plan.ts`: `homePlan(home)`, the home as a builder's `Plan` with every choice spelled (the Glances strip, each room, person and system tile by its slots, the cars by key, the sections' titles as their looks, `popupOpen` as `open`), and `systemChoices(home)`, the system tiles in their order, which `problems()` reads too.
- `view.ts`: `build(home)`, `homePlan(home)` drawn by `dashboardOf()` with no registries, so nothing is discovered: one `sections` view of `custom:mnml-template-card` instances, every slot spelled and no `area`, the Glances strip and the sections one under another, and the popups card; `drawn(home)`, the same dashboard as the templates expand it, which is what a tool that checks entity ids reads. It expands with the shipped templates only; a home's shared templates are seen by the cards, not by `drawn()`.
- `problems.ts`: `problems(home)`, what would break the dashboard without failing its build: a hash opened that no pop-up defines, a hash defined or producible twice, a key that is no URL fragment, a subnet that is no IPv4 range. A home's tests assert it is empty.

## `src/builder/`: the dashboard builder

What the panel's builder and the dashboard strategy make a dashboard from. It is pure: it reads the home's registries and the templates it is given, so it runs in the panel and in Node alike.

- `plan.ts`: `planFrom(dashboardTemplate, registries, templates)` refills a dashboard template in a home: the areas that are rooms where the rooms section's template draws, every person, the system section's templates whose entities discovery finds, no car, and the sections' looks. `DEFAULT_DASHBOARD_TEMPLATE` is the shipped one, and `defaultPlan(registries, templates)`, the quick start, is it refilled: the areas that are rooms where the room template draws something beyond the area's name and icon, in the order Home Assistant lists them; every `person` entity; each of `SYSTEM_TEMPLATES` whose required slots discovery fills over the whole home; pop-ups that unfold on tablet and desktop.
- In `plan.ts`, `areaKinds(registries)` tells each area's kind from one table of marks on its entities: `room` when it holds something a room shows, otherwise `phones`, `system` or `empty`, by its devices. Each mark of `MARKS` is a discovery filter, which `matches()` of `filters.ts` reads as it reads a template's rule, on the integration, domain, device class, translation key, entity category or an attribute. A temperature or humidity sensor's mark also asks that a device measures it, a device that is no service, or that it is the area's own, and a power sensor's that its device has a switch. `unplaced(registries)` counts what a room would show that is in no area: the devices in no area that hold it, the entities on no device, and their share of all a room would show ([Building a dashboard](editors.md#building-a-dashboard)). The room test (`MARKS`, `areaKinds()`, `unplaced()`) reads each area's entities against one table of marks; a `device_tracker` moves only with `source_type: gps`.
- `person.ts`: `personOf(registries, entity)`, a person's slots: the key from the entity id, and one device per tracker in the person's `device_trackers` that the companion app (`mobile_app`) made, with the app's sensors on that device by their entity ids' endings (`_battery_level`, `_battery_state`, `_connection_type`, `_ssid`, `_storage`, `_focus`, `_activity`, `_location_permission`). A tracker that lacks one of them is left out, and a person with none is the person entity alone.
- `customized.ts`: from a card its editor changed back to the plan: `roomFrom()` (the area picked, the overrides), `personFrom()` and `systemFrom()` (only what differs from what MNML finds, by `overridesOf()`), and `carFrom()`, a spelled row staying spelled (the key out of the slots, or no car without one that is a name).
- `dashboard-template.ts`: `dashboardTemplateOf(plan, templates, shipped)`, a dashboard template from a plan. It holds the sections the plan has (one with something, or with a look), their looks, the system templates chosen, the openings, and every template it uses, inside others too, that is not the shipped one as shipped, whole. `dashboardTemplateText()` writes it under `mnml_dashboard:`. `readDashboardTemplate(text, shipped)` reads one, refusing a dashboard's configuration, a set of templates, an unknown section, or a section template neither shipped nor bundled, with the reason. `renamedDashboardTemplate()` follows the names its templates come in under.
- `dashboard.ts`: `dashboardOf(plan, registries, templates)`, one `sections` view with a heading and the cards of each part that has any (Rooms, Devices, People, Garage, System, in the plan's `order`), each heading and template from the section's look, and the popups card. The Glances strip comes first, across the view, then the sections, one under another. A spelled choice is its slots alone. A room is its `area`, discovered live, with its overrides; a person is `personOf()` with the overrides over it; a car is its slots and key. A device is a template card with its `template` and `device` (`deviceCard()`); a device that is gone is left out. `roomCard()`, `personCard()`, `carCard()` and `systemCard()` make each card alone, for the builder's rows.
- In `dashboard.ts`, a system template without overrides is the template alone and discovers live; with them, it holds what discovery found when the plan was built, and the overrides over it, since a card that spells slots does not discover. Every card holds only the slots and fields its template declares, a retired one dropped too; an area room left with none has no `slots`. `roomCard()`, `personCard()` and `carCard()` take the templates as an optional last argument.
- `parts.ts`: `partsOf(template)`, the slots a tile's top-level parts draw only when filled, in the card's order, without a required slot or a part drawn for each item; `swapsFor(registries, entity, area)`, the other entities of its domain and device class, its device's first, then its area's, then the rest, each by id.
- `devices.ts`: `offersIn()`, the devices a template stands for, by area in Home Assistant's order, then those in no area, each with its cards best first; `roomFound()`; `shownBy()`, the room of the plan that holds one of a device's own entities.
- `areas.ts`: the area assistant's suggestions ([Sorting the home into areas](editors.md#sorting-the-home-into-areas)). `suggestAreas(registries, rooms)` reads each device in no area by its name, and each entity on no device and in no area by its registry name, friendly name and object id. `wordsOf()` makes words of them, in lower case and without accents.
- In `areas.ts`, a subject takes the earliest, then longest, run of words that is an area's name, id or alias. A device that finds none takes the area most of its entities find. What finds none is read against `rooms`, and a room word that two subjects or more find is a new area (`create`).
- `areas.ts` also holds `groupedByArea()`, Home Assistant's areas in its order and then the new ones, and `placedRegistries()`, the registries as the suggestions would leave them, a new area's id from `newAreaId()`.
- `strategy.ts`: `strategyPlan(config, registries, templates)`, the plan of a `custom:mnml` strategy: the quick start's plan, each key the strategy's options name in place of its own, `type` aside. Options that make no plan are refused, each key that does not fit named (`MNML strategy: rooms is not a dashboard choice`).
- `openings.ts`: the words for how a pop-up opens (`OPENING_WORDS`) on each screen (`SCREEN_WORDS`, with what each gets by default), for the editors that choose it.

## `src/strategy/`: the dashboard strategy

A dashboard made from the plan each time Home Assistant shows it, so it follows the home: an area, a person or a system's entities added appear without a rebuild. The dashboard's configuration is `strategy: { type: custom:mnml }` and the plan's choices beside `type` ([The dashboard strategy](home.md#the-dashboard-strategy)).

- `strategy.ts`: `MnmlStrategy`, the element `register.ts` defines as `ll-strategy-dashboard-mnml`; Home Assistant calls only its static members. `generate(config, hass)` waits for every shipped family and for the integration's store, then reads the energy settings (`energyPrefs()`), and returns `dashboardOf()` of `strategyPlan()` over `hass`'s registries and those settings, with the templates as a card reads them (`resolvedTemplates()`). A family that cannot be loaded, or a store that cannot be read, fails the dashboard with the reason, which Home Assistant shows in its place. Since the families are loaded by then, the template cards of the dashboard expand at once. `registryDependencies` (areas, devices and entities) makes Home Assistant generate it again when one of them changes. `getCreateSuggestions()` offers the quick start's title and icon in the dialog that adds the dashboard, and `getConfigElement()` the editor. `homeTemplates(hass)` is the waiting, which the editor shares.
- `editor.ts`: `MnmlStrategyEditor`, the strategy's editor in the dashboard's settings. For the rooms, the people and the system cards it offers either what MNML finds, named, or a choice of its own, which starts from what MNML finds, each shown or not and moved up or down. A chosen room, person or system card keeps its slots, and a spelled one is listed by its name. It also edits the Glances strip, and how pop-ups open on each screen. Each change is sent whole (`config-changed`), the keys left as they were kept. Cars, the title, the icon, the sections' looks and the order are written in YAML.

Taking control, in Home Assistant's dashboard menu, saves what the strategy last generated without the strategy: a dashboard like one the panel builds, whose cards discover as they did and which no longer follows the home.

## `custom_components/mnml/`: the integration

One config entry (`single_config_entry`), no devices and no entities. Its flow asks the two options, the glass design and MNML as the default theme, and the options form asks them again.

- `__init__.py`: `async_setup_entry()`: the stores, then the websocket commands, the frontend, the panel, the theme and the repairs, the default theme, the options listener. Each step that puts something on the pages registers its undo with `entry.async_on_unload()` as soon as it is done, and Home Assistant runs those undos on unload and when setup fails, so a later step that fails leaves no loader and no panel behind. The options' defaults are `DEFAULT_GLASS` and `DEFAULT_DEFAULT_THEME` in `const.py`. `async_unload_entry()` takes the bundle and the panel off the pages and clears the repairs; `async_remove_entry()` deletes the theme and gives the default theme back
- In `__init__.py`, `MnmlData` (whether the glass design is on) is the entry's runtime data; the options listener swaps the theme when the design changes. The default theme option is what is wanted, and the entry's data keeps what was last applied (`applied_default_theme`): at setup and on every change of the options, `async_sync_default()` makes MNML the default theme, or gives the default back, when the two differ, and makes it the default only while Home Assistant loads MNML's theme. So an answer of the setup form, or an option turned on before the theme loads, takes effect at the first setup that finds the theme, and a start with nothing changed leaves a default chosen since in Home Assistant alone
- `frontend.py`: `loader_url(www)`, `/mnml-files/mnml-cards-loader.js?v=<first 8 of the sha256 of the loader and the bundle>`, which fails setup with `ConfigEntryError`, naming what is missing, when the loader, the bundle, the panel or one of the two themes (`mnml.yaml`, `mnml-flat.yaml`) is not built. `async_register_frontend()` serves `www/` at `/mnml-files/` with long cache headers (once per Home Assistant run) and adds the loader to every page with `add_extra_js_url`. Home Assistant's static path serves a file's `.br` sibling to a browser whose `Accept-Encoding` takes `br`, else its `.gz` sibling to one that takes `gzip`, else the file itself, with the file's own content type, `Content-Encoding` and `Vary: Accept-Encoding`. The build writes both siblings from the same bytes, so the digest of the loader and the bundle covers them too. The URL comes off the pages on unload, and when a later step of setup fails
- `theme.py`: `write_theme()` writes a built theme to `themes/mnml-integration/mnml.yaml`, atomically, when it differs. `async_install_theme(glass=)` chooses `www/mnml.yaml` or, flat, `www/mnml-flat.yaml`, and then reloads themes, and when Home Assistant does not load a theme named MNML from it (no `themes` include, an include of another folder, or `!include_dir_named`, which cannot hold it) takes the folder away again, so the configuration stays valid. A reload that fails is tried again without the folder: when that one succeeds, the file was the cause and stays away; when it fails too, the cause is elsewhere (an error in `configuration.yaml`), so the file is written back, the failure is logged and no repair is raised, and the theme loads at Home Assistant's next reload or restart
- In `theme.py`, `theme_loaded()` says whether Home Assistant holds a theme named MNML, and `other_theme_files()` finds another file under `themes/` that defines MNML, the standalone theme from HACS in `themes/mnml/` included. `async_apply_default()` sets MNML as the default theme in light and dark mode, or, turned off, gives back each mode MNML still holds (`none`); it logs a change Home Assistant refuses rather than raising it. `async_remove_theme()` deletes the folder and reloads themes, which also gives back a default that named MNML
- `conflicts.py`: `async_hand_loaded()`: the URL of a Lovelace resource, stored in the UI or in YAML, that loads `mnml-cards.js` from anywhere but `/mnml-files/`. It reads Lovelace's resource collection, which is not a promised API, and answers nothing when that collection is not what it expects
- `dashboards.py`: `DashboardStore`: the dashboards the panel's builder made, in `.storage/mnml.dashboards`, by their `url_path`: each one's plan, its last save's time and user, and the version a rebuild replaced (its plan and its Lovelace configuration), which an undo restores; `Built` and `Previous` type them. `DASHBOARD_STORE` is its key in `hass.data`, loaded beside the templates' store; one that cannot be read is logged and left out, and its commands answer `not_loaded`
- `issues.py`: the three repairs, raised or cleared on every setup: `theme_not_loaded`, `second_theme`, `hand_loaded_bundle`
- `store.py`: `TemplateStore`: the home's templates in `.storage/mnml.templates`, through Home Assistant's storage helper, each with its last save's time and user and its previous 10 versions; listeners are told after each write. `Saved` types what a save sends, `Kept` a template as kept, and `Deleted` what a delete leaves: the versions alone. `STORE` is its key in `hass.data`, loaded on the first setup of a run, before the cards are served, so a page that loads them finds the store ready. A store that cannot be read is logged and left out: setup goes on, the websocket answers `not_loaded`, and the cards draw the shipped templates
- `panel.py`: `async_register_panel()`, the MNML panel at `/mnml` for admins, with the icon `mnml:mnml`, from `www/mnml-cards-panel.js` named by its content; `async_remove_panel()` on unload
- `websocket.py`: `mnml/templates/subscribe` (every user: the set, then the set again after each save and delete), `save`, `delete` and `history` (admins), and `mnml/dashboards/list`, `save` and `delete` (admins), registered once per run. A dashboard's `save` takes a plan of the shape of `isPlan()`, and the version it replaces, at a `url_path` of lower case letters and digits with a hyphen between them, as Home Assistant's own dashboards have, at most 512 kB each and 100 in all. The template commands make the shape checks of [Templates](templates.md#where-templates-live), and keep at most 500 templates
- `config_flow.py`: the flow, whose one form asks Use the glass design (on, `DEFAULT_GLASS`) and Use MNML as the default theme (off, `DEFAULT_DEFAULT_THEME`), and the options form, which asks the same two
- `translations/en.json`: every string Home Assistant shows: the flow, the option, the repairs
- `brand/`: the icons, drawn as `icon-light.svg` and `icon-dark.svg`; `pnpm icons` renders each to a PNG of 256 and 512 px with transparent corners: `icon.png` and `icon@2x.png` from the light one, `dark_icon.png` and `dark_icon@2x.png` from the dark one. Home Assistant serves them for the integration, the logo names falling back to the icon of the same theme, and HACS's brand check finds `icon.png`

**Why a loader.** Home Assistant imports an extra module as soon as its page starts, before its app has installed the scoped custom-element registry it runs on. A card class declared before that extends the browser's own `HTMLElement` and cannot be constructed afterwards. So the page gets `mnml-cards-loader.js` (`src/cards/loader.ts`), which waits until `home-assistant` is defined (`src/cards/started.ts`) and then imports `mnml-cards.js` with its own `?v=`; on a page where Home Assistant already runs it imports at once. Before it waits, the loader registers the `mnml` icon set (`src/cards/iconset.ts`) in `window.customIcons`, as Home Assistant's frontend reads it: `mnml:mnml` is the logo's frame made square, with M and N on the first row and M and the corner on the second, one 24 px path in the colour of wherever it is drawn. Being early, it is there before the sidebar draws the panel's icon.

`/mnml-files/` and not `/mnml/`: the panel takes `/mnml`. `themes/mnml-integration/` and not `themes/mnml/`: HACS installs the standalone MNML Theme there. An update of the integration takes effect after a restart, as for any integration; a reload of the entry serves a rebuilt `www/` under a new `?v=`.

## `demo/`: the demo

- `home.ts`: `DEMO`, a home of nine rooms, Joe and Jane, two cars and the six systems, which draws every template. The demo integration supplies its climates, media players, calendars, camera, vacuum, weather, lock and the kitchen's lights, under their own ids.
- `main.ts` writes `out/demo.yaml`; `tools/dashboard.ts` saves the same dashboard as `mnml-demo` on the throwaway instance.
- `traits.ts`: each demo entity's name, icon (by state where it changes), unit, device class and reading, taken once from the home the demo was made from, with the same names and words scrubbed as in `home.ts`.
- `states.ts`: what makes the demo lived in: the rooms whose lights are off, the rooms heating, who is away, and a few states set outright (an open window, a low and a critical battery, an unlocked car, a stopped guest, a print running).
- `entities.ts`: `packageOf(home)`, a Home Assistant package of template entities, scenes, scripts, helpers and generic thermostats for every id the home draws that the demo integration does not supply, from the traits and the states. It adds a `customize` block that names and icons the demo integration's entities, the scenes and the thermostats (`customizeOf()`). Run, it writes `.ha/packages/demo.yaml` and copies the QR, map and 3D printer images to `.ha/www/`. `created()` lists the ids a package makes, and its test holds the two together.
- `tools/demo.ts` writes the `customize` names and icons to the registry too, for the entities that have an entry, since a card reads a registered entity's name from the registry. It adds the people and their device trackers, home or away, and the 3D printer's camera from its image. It gives each numeric template sensor a display precision of as many decimals as its reading, and renames what Home Assistant kept from an earlier run. It removes the demo's entities the package does not make, and fails on an id another integration took first, which belongs in `SUPPLIED`.

## `src/build/`: the build

- `buildBundle(file)` is one rolldown build for the browser, of minified ES modules written beside `file`. Three entries keep fixed names: `mnml-cards.js`, the bundle (`src/cards/register.ts`); `mnml-cards-loader.js` (`src/cards/loader.ts`); and `mnml-cards-panel.js` (`src/panel/main.ts`), which the integration registers, and whose `yaml` package reaches no dashboard.
- **The card editors** (`src/editors/main.ts`) are a chunk of their own, `mnml-cards-editors-<hash>.js`, which nothing imports statically. The build fills the generated module `src/editors/where.ts` with its URL, and a card imports it from its `getConfigElement()` (`src/cards/edit.ts`). The URL is a module of its own on purpose: a browser keeps a failed dynamic import for the page, so a retry asks for the same file under a fresh URL, `?attempt=<n>`. The editors carry no YAML parser, since Home Assistant's own YAML tab covers YAML.
- **Shared chunks.** What several entries share is a chunk named by its content, `mnml-cards-<name>-<hash>.js`.
- **The literals are minified.** A plugin runs `minify-literals` (lightningcss for the styles, html-minifier-next for the markup) over every file under `src/` that holds a `css`, `html` or `svg` template.
- **The families.** `common.yaml` goes in as data. Every other family is written beside the bundle as `mnml-cards-<family>.json`, and the bundle names each by its content (`?v=<hash>`), since the integration serves them with long cache headers.
- **Compressed siblings.** Every script and family a page loads, each `.js` and `.json`, gets a `.br` (brotli at its best quality) and a `.gz` (gzip at level 9) beside it, of the same bytes, compressed side by side once everything is written. Home Assistant's static path serves the one the browser takes ([The integration](#custom_componentsmnml-the-integration)). A browser asks for `br` over HTTPS only, so a home on plain HTTP gets the `.gz`. The source maps, which only a browser's developer tools fetch, stay plain: their siblings would add about 0.9 MB to `mnml.zip` and 2 s to the build.
- **A build starts clean.** It first removes every file of the folder whose name starts with the bundle's stem (`mnml-cards`), so no chunk of an earlier build stays beside the new ones.
- **Each map is named by its content.** Every file has its source map beside it, sources included, so a browser's developer tools show the TypeScript and a stack trace names it. The file's last line is `//# sourceMappingURL=<file>.map?v=<hash>`, the map's own hash. The files are served with long cache headers, so a fixed name could pair a new file with an older map; a new map is a new URL. Its paths are relative to this repository (`src/...`), and a dependency's start at its package (`node_modules/lit-html/...`) wherever the package manager keeps it, so a build inside a parent workspace writes the maps a checkout of its own does.
- `node src/build/main.ts [out]` writes them into `out` (resolved from the working directory), the bundle under the name `src/build/names.ts` gives; `pnpm run build:frontend` gives it `custom_components/mnml/www/`, and a project that holds MNML as a submodule builds into its own folder.
- `node src/theme/main.ts [out]` writes `mnml.yaml` (glass) and `mnml-flat.yaml` there, after every contrast claim of both holds; `pnpm run build:theme` gives it the same folder. `pnpm build` runs both.

## Releases

`.github/workflows/check.yml` runs on every pull request and every push to `main`, as jobs that run side by side, each on its own runner: `lint` (oxfmt, oxlint, markdownlint, knip), `typescript` (vitest), `python` (ruff, ruff format, mypy), `pytest`, `hassfest`, `floor` (the Python tests on the oldest Home Assistant supported) and `hacs` (HACS's validation). Together they run every step of `pnpm check`, and `build.test.ts` fails when a step of it is in no job.
